subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: LiDAR: Peeling Back the Jungle
description: A short lesson to help you apply LiDAR: Peeling Back the Jungle.

hook.text: A laser technology that can see through dense forest canopy is rewriting the history of entire civilizations.

buildup.text: LiDAR fires millions of laser pulses from aircraft. Some pass through leaves and bounce off the ground below.

discovery.text: In Cambodia, LiDAR revealed that Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city on Earth — far bigger than maps showed.

twist.text: In Guatemala, it found 60,000 Maya structures, roads, and farms that no one had seen despite decades of ground surveys.

climax.text: LiDAR is finding so many sites so fast that there are not enough archaeologists to investigate them all.

punchline.text: We spent centuries searching jungles on foot. Lasers did more in a week.

quiz.question: What did LiDAR reveal about the Maya civilization in Guatemala?
options: The Maya had no roads or infrastructure between cities
60,000 structures, roads, and farms invisible from ground surveys
Maya cities were much smaller than previously estimated
